imc-1995-01.prompt: Let $X$ be a nonsingular matrix with columns $X_1,X_2,\dots,X_n$. Let $Y$ be the matrix with columns $X_2,X_3,\dots,X_n,0$. Show that the matrices $A=YX^{-1}$ and $B=X^{-1}Y$ have rank $n-1$ and have only $0$'s for eigenvalues.
imc-1995-01.answer: $Y=XJ$, where $J$ is the nilpotent shift matrix ($Je_j=e_{j+1}$, $Je_n=0$). So $B=J$ and $A=XJX^{-1}$ is similar to $J$, which has rank $n-1$ and only the eigenvalue $0$.

imc-1995-02.prompt:
Let $f$ be a continuous function on $[0,1]$ such that for every $x\in[0,1]$ we have $\displaystyle\int_x^1 f(t)\,dt\ge\frac{1-x^2}{2}$. Show that
$$\int_0^1 f^2(t)\,dt\ge\frac13 .$$
imc-1995-02.answer: Integrate the hypothesis over $x\in[0,1]$ and swap the order: $\int_0^1 tf(t)\,dt\ge\frac13$. Then $0\le\int_0^1(f-x)^2$ (or Cauchy–Schwarz) gives $\int f^2\ge2\int xf-\frac13\ge\frac13$.

imc-1995-03.prompt:
Let $f$ be twice continuously differentiable on $(0,+\infty)$ such that $\lim\limits_{x\to0+}f'(x)=-\infty$ and $\lim\limits_{x\to0+}f''(x)=+\infty$. Show that
$$\lim_{x\to0+}\frac{f(x)}{f'(x)}=0 .$$
imc-1995-03.answer: Near $0$, $f'<0$ is increasing, so for $0<x<x_0$: $0<f(x)-f(x_0)\le(x_0-x)|f'(x)|$. Dividing by $f'(x)\to-\infty$ gives $-x_0\le\liminf\frac{f}{f'}\le\limsup\frac{f}{f'}\le0$; then let $x_0\to0$.

imc-1995-04.prompt:
Let $F:(1,\infty)\to\mathbb R$ be the function defined by
$$F(x)=\int_x^{x^2}\frac{dt}{\ln t}.$$
Show that $F$ is one-to-one (i.e. injective) and find the range (i.e. set of values) of $F$.
imc-1995-04.answer: $F'(x)=\frac{x-1}{\ln x}>0$, so $F$ is strictly increasing. With $t=e^v$, $F(x)=\int_{\ln x}^{2\ln x}\frac{e^v}{v}dv$ lies strictly between $x\ln2$ and $x^2\ln2$. The range is $(\ln2,\infty)$.

imc-1995-05.prompt:
Let $A$ and $B$ be real $n\times n$ matrices. Assume that there exist $n+1$ different real numbers $t_1,t_2,\dots,t_{n+1}$ such that the matrices
$$C_i=A+t_iB,\qquad i=1,2,\dots,n+1,$$
are nilpotent (i.e. $C_i^n=0$). Show that both $A$ and $B$ are nilpotent.
imc-1995-05.answer: $(A+tB)^n=A^n+tP_1+\dots+t^{n-1}P_{n-1}+t^nB^n$. Each entry is a polynomial in $t$ of degree $\le n$ with $n+1$ roots, so it is identically zero. In particular $A^n=B^n=0$.

imc-1995-06.prompt:
Let $p>1$. Show that there exists a constant $K_p>0$ such that for every $x,y\in\mathbb R$ satisfying $|x|^p+|y|^p=2$ we have
$$(x-y)^2\le K_p\big(4-(x+y)^2\big).$$
imc-1995-06.answer: The denominator $4-(x+y)^2$ vanishes on the curve only at $(1,1)$ and $(-1,-1)$ (strict power-mean inequality), so compactness handles everything away from these points. Near $(1,1)$, Taylor's formula for $t^p$ gives $2\ge2s^p+md^2$ with $s=\frac{x+y}2$, $d=\frac{x-y}2$, hence $1-s\ge\frac{m}{2p}d^2$.

imc-1995-08.prompt:
Let $\{b_n\}_{n=0}^\infty$ be a sequence of positive real numbers such that $b_0=1$ and
$$b_n=2+\sqrt{b_{n-1}}-2\sqrt{1+\sqrt{b_{n-1}}}.$$
Calculate
$$\sum_{n=1}^\infty b_n2^n .$$

imc-1995-09.prompt:
Let all roots of an $n$-th degree polynomial $P(z)$ with complex coefficients lie on the unit circle in the complex plane. Prove that all roots of the polynomial
$$2zP'(z)-nP(z)$$
lie on the same circle.
imc-1995-09.answer: For $P(z)\ne0$: $\dfrac{2zP'(z)-nP(z)}{P(z)}=\sum_k\dfrac{z+\alpha_k}{z-\alpha_k}$, whose real part is $\sum_k\dfrac{|z|^2-1}{|z-\alpha_k|^2}$. This is non-zero when $|z|\ne1$.

imc-1995-10.prompt:
a) Prove that for every $\varepsilon>0$ there is a positive integer $n$ and real numbers $\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_n$ such that
$$\max_{x\in[-1,1]}\Big|x-\sum_{k=1}^n\lambda_kx^{2k+1}\Big|<\varepsilon .$$

b) Prove that for every odd continuous function $f$ on $[-1,1]$ and for every $\varepsilon>0$ there is a positive integer $n$ and real numbers $\mu_1,\dots,\mu_n$ such that
$$\max_{x\in[-1,1]}\Big|f(x)-\sum_{k=1}^n\mu_kx^{2k+1}\Big|<\varepsilon .$$
(Recall that $f$ is odd means that $f(x)=-f(-x)$ for all $x\in[-1,1]$.)
imc-1995-10.answer: a) $x-\sum_{k=1}^n(-1)^{k+1}\binom nk x^{2k+1}=x(1-x^2)^n$, which is uniformly small for large $n$. b) Weierstrass gives an odd polynomial $q$ close to $f$; replace its linear term $b_0x$ using a).

imc-1995-11.prompt:
a) Prove that every function of the form
$$f(x)=\frac{a_0}{2}+\cos x+\sum_{n=2}^Na_n\cos(nx)$$
with $|a_0|<1$ has positive as well as negative values in the period $[0,2\pi)$.

b) Prove that the function
$$F(x)=\sum_{n=1}^{100}\cos\big(n^{3/2}x\big)$$
has at least $40$ zeros in the interval $(0,1000)$.
imc-1995-11.answer: a) $\int_0^{2\pi}f(x)(1\pm\cos x)\,dx=\pi(a_0\pm1)$. b) If $F$ kept one sign on an interval $(y,y+h)$, then $\left|\int F\cos x\right|\le\left|\int F\right|$. But $\left|\int F\right|<6$, while $\left|\int F\cos x\right|>\frac h2-6$. So $F$ changes sign on every interval of length $24$, and $(0,1000)$ contains $41$ disjoint such intervals.

imc-1995-12.prompt:
Suppose that $\{f_n\}_{n=1}^\infty$ is a sequence of continuous functions on the interval $[0,1]$ such that
$$\int_0^1f_m(x)f_n(x)\,dx=\begin{cases}1&\text{if }n=m\\0&\text{if }n\ne m\end{cases}$$
and
$$\sup\{|f_n(x)|:x\in[0,1]\text{ and }n=1,2,\dots\}<+\infty .$$
Show that there exists no subsequence $\{f_{n_k}\}$ of $\{f_n\}$ such that $\lim\limits_{k\to\infty}f_{n_k}(x)$ exists for all $x\in[0,1]$.
imc-1995-12.answer: If $f_{n_k}\to f$ pointwise, dominated convergence (the functions are uniformly bounded) gives $\int(f_{n_k}-f_{n_{k+1}})^2\to0$. But by orthonormality this integral equals $2$ for every $k$.
